$comment: Hand-written Strudel reference entries, merged over the generated ones by tools/gen-strudel-ref.mjs. A value of null drops an entry. midi and osc are Uaithne's own implementations (WebKitGTK has no WebMIDI; there's no Node OSC bridge), and the inline visuals are drawn by Uaithne.

params.name: output
params.doc: optional: an output port's name, or part of it (case doesn't matter). Without one, the output chosen in Settings (Ctrl+,) is used, else the first one.

midi.synopsis: Plays the pattern on a MIDI output instead of Strudel's own sounds.
midi.description:
Each event's `note` is sent as a note on, and its note off follows after the event's length. `velocity` (default 0.9) times `gain` sets the velocity. `midichan` picks the channel (1–16), `ccn` with `ccv` (0–1) sends a control change, and `progNum` a program change. `midiport` picks the output per event, like the argument.

In Uaithne, MIDI goes out through the system (ALSA on Linux), timed to line up with the audio. Pick a default output in Settings (`Ctrl+,`).

osc.synopsis: Sends each event as an OSC message, to SuperDirt by default.
osc.description:
Each event goes out as `address key value key value …` with all of its controls, plus `cps`, `cycle` and `delta` (seconds), in a bundle timestamped for when it should play. The target is set in Settings (`Ctrl+,`); it's SuperDirt (`127.0.0.1:57120`) to begin with, so a pattern with `.osc()` plays through SuperCollider, the same engine as Tidal. `oscport` sends to another port on this machine.

Strudel's `note` (a MIDI number) is sent as `midinote`, since SuperDirt's `note` counts from middle C. Tidal must be running for SuperDirt to hear it.

_pianoroll.synopsis: Shows a visual right under its line in the editor, instead of in the visuals panel.
_pianoroll.description: Every visual has an inline form with a leading underscore: `._pianoroll()`, `._punchcard()`, `._wordfall()`, `._spiral()`, `._pitchwheel()`, `._scope()`, `._fscope()` and `._spectrum()`. Each draws on its own canvas under the line where it's called, and moves with the code as you edit. They take the same options as the plain forms, plus `height` (and `width`) in pixels. The plain forms (`.pianoroll()` …) draw in the visuals panel (`Ctrl+J`), one beside the other.
